title: A geologist's wedding gift was a pink diamond

hook.text: The Queen's wedding gift: a pink diamond.

end.line: A new jewelry story every day

lines.text: The Queen's wedding gift: a pink diamond.
In 1947, John Williamson's mine in Tanganyika produced a pink diamond.
lines.say: In nineteen forty-seven, John Williamson's mine in Tanganyika produced a pink diamond.

lines.text: Williamson, a Canadian geologist, gave it to Princess Elizabeth
as a wedding present for her and Prince Philip.
It was 54.5 carats in the rough,
lines.say: It was fifty-four point five carats in the rough,

lines.text: and two London cutters made it a 23.6-carat round brilliant.
lines.say: and two London cutters made it a twenty-three point six carat round brilliant.

lines.text: Cartier set it in a platinum brooch shaped like a jonquil flower,
with 203 small white diamonds around it.
lines.say: with two hundred three small white diamonds around it.

lines.text: The brooch was finished in 1953, her coronation year.
lines.say: The brooch was finished in nineteen fifty-three, her coronation year.

lines.text: In 2024, Queen Camilla wore it to a Buckingham Palace garden party.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-four, Queen Camilla wore it to a Buckingham Palace garden party.

post.caption: In 1947 Canadian geologist John Williamson gave Princess Elizabeth a pink diamond from his Tanganyika mine as a wedding present. Cut to 23.6 carats and set by Cartier as a jonquil brooch, it was worn by Queen Camilla in 2024.
